title: $\mathcal{H}$olographic $\mathcal{N}$aturalness and Information See-Saw Mechanism for Neutrinos
summary: The microscopic origin of the de Sitter entropy remains a central puzzle in quantum gravity related to the cosmological constant problem. Within $\mathcal{H}$olographic $\mathcal{N}$aturalness, we propose this entropy is carried by light, coherent degrees of freedom - "hairons" - emerging as moduli of gravitational instantons on orbifolds. From the Euclidean de Sitter instanton ($S^4$), we construct a new class of orbifold gravitational instantons, $S^4/\mathbb{Z}_N$, where $N$ corresponds to the de Sitter entropy. The moduli space dimension scales linearly with $N$, and we identify these moduli with hairon fields. A $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry from Wilson loops ensures mode distinguishability, yielding the correct entropy. Hairons acquire a mass of the order of the Hubble scale with negligible interactions, suggesting the de Sitter vacuum is a Bose-Einstein condensate of these excitations. We then unify the neutrino mass generation with the cosmological constant via gravitational topology. The small neutrino mass emerges naturally without new physics beyond the Standard Model. The gravitational Chern-Simons structure and anomaly force a topological Higgs mechanism, leading to neutrino condensation via $S^4/\mathbb{Z}_N$ instantons. The topological degrees $N \sim M_\text{P}^2/Λ\sim 10^{120}$ provide both a holographic entropy counting and a $1/N$ information see-saw mechanism for neutrino masses. Predictions: (i) neutrino superfluid condensation forming Cooper pairs below meV as cold dark matter; (ii) resolution of the strong CP problem via a QCD composite axion; (iii) time-varying neutrino masses tracking th dark energy evolution; (iv) signatures in astroparticle physics, ultra-high-energy cosmic rays and high magnetic field experiments.

AI.tldr: The paper explores the de Sitter entropy's origin in quantum gravity, proposing 'hairons' as key degrees of freedom, and unifying neutrino mass generation with the cosmological constant using gravitational topology.
AI.motivation: To address the mystery of de Sitter entropy and its link to the cosmological constant problem in quantum gravity.
AI.method: Construct new orbifold gravitational instantons ($S^4/	ext{Z}_N$) and identify moduli as hairon fields; apply gravitational topology to unify neutrino mass generation and the cosmological constant.
AI.result: Demonstrates a mass scale for hairons near the Hubble scale, suggests the de Sitter vacuum acts as a Bose-Einstein condensate, and provides predictions for neutrino behavior and dark matter.
AI.conclusion: The findings connect de Sitter entropy to neutrino mass generation, suggesting profound implications for dark matter, the strong CP problem, and cosmological observations.

title: Chiral-Transport-Induced Collective Modes in Strong Magnetic Fields and Their Implications for Neutron Star Phenomenology
summary: In this thesis, we study the collective modes induced by the chirality of elementary particles in magnetized media and their implications for neutron star phenomenology. We theoretically predict that the chiral magnetic wave can arise in quark matter inside neutron stars, resulting in the emergence of novel types of seismic oscillations and associated gravitational waves in the context of asteroseismology. We also investigate the response to dynamical electromagnetic fields and find that a dynamical screening, distinct from the conventional Landau damping, occurs due to the chiral anomaly.

AI.tldr: This thesis explores the effects of chirality in magnetized media on neutron stars, predicting the existence of chiral magnetic waves and their implications for seismic oscillations and gravitational waves, as well as a unique dynamical screening effect linked to the chiral anomaly.
AI.motivation: Understanding the collective modes and phenomena related to chirality in neutron stars can enhance insights into their behavior and characteristics in astrophysical contexts.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis of chiral magnetic waves and their impact on quark matter within neutron stars, examining induced seismic oscillations and the response to electromagnetic fields.
AI.result: Prediction of novel seismic oscillations and gravitational waves arising from chiral magnetic waves, alongside identification of a new dynamical screening effect related to the chiral anomaly.
AI.conclusion: The findings could significantly advance the understanding of neutron star physics, particularly in the realm of asteroseismology and the role of chirality in astrophysical contexts.

title: Naturally Resonant Emitters: Approaching Fundamental Antenna Limits
summary: Antenna miniaturization remains a critical technological challenge across frequency scales - from microwave RF links in phones and wearables to VLF for underwater-to-air communications and ionospheric probing. At deeply subwavelength scales conventional antennas require complex and lossy matching circuits due to absent intrinsic material resonances, motivating resonant electrically small emitters (ESEs) like mechanical resonators and quantum emitters. Here, we extend the theory of electrically small antennas (ESAs) to this broader ESE class, deriving the fundamental efficiency limit for a unit volume emitter at given frequency and bandwidth. Our figure of merit (FOM) - quantifying proximity to this limit - enables direct comparison across ESE types, frequencies, bandwidths and scales. We demonstrate its utility using public data from ELF and VLF Navy facilities alongside two mechanical ESEs reported in literature. The measurements reveal that mechanical antennas operate near theoretical FOM limit, questioning claims of possible further orders-of-magnitude gains. A naturally resonant emitter is still subject to the Chu-Harrington limit (CHL) under its standard assumptions. Indeed, we derive novel CHL-dictated constraints on atomic ESE properties: lower bound on excited-state lifetime and an upper bound on transition dipole moment.

AI.tldr: The paper extends antenna theory to electrically small emitters (ESEs), deriving efficiency limits and comparing various ESE types, revealing that mechanical ESEs operate near theoretical limits.
AI.motivation: To address challenges in antenna miniaturization across various frequency scales and improve efficiency in small emitters.
AI.method: The authors extend existing theories of electrically small antennas to derive efficiency limits and create a figure of merit for different ESE types, utilizing public Navy data and literature examples for validation.
AI.result: The study shows that mechanical antennas operate close to the theoretical efficiency limit, challenging notions of further significant gains, and establishes constraints on atomic ESE properties based on Chu-Harrington principles.
AI.conclusion: While resonant emitters approach limits, they are still constrained by fundamental principles, indicating a ceiling on potential improvements in ESE technology.

title: Mesogenesis through the Ephemeral Dark Decay of Beauty
summary: Mesogenesis provides a path for generating the baryon asymmetry of the Universe, using only the CP violation furnished by the Standard Model in the decay of $B$ mesons. While this is an intriguing possibility, it is largely constrained by the data on $B$ meson branching fractions into baryons and missing energy carried into the dark sector. We point out that it is possible to make this branching fraction dominant only in the early Universe, through an ultralight scalar coupled to the dark sector and the Standard Model leptons. A scenario is examined where the thermal density of muons in the early Universe temporarily lowers the mass of a dark fermion, allowing for efficient $B$ meson decays. This `dark' decay channel is shut off later when the muon number density falls, making the scenario compatible with flavor data. Our model can be consistent with the LHC constraints on color-charged heavy bosons required to implement Mesogenesis; such states may be discovered in the future runs as their masses cannot be far above the current bounds. We also outline other possible signals, which can arise in future flavor data, long range force searches, and observations of neutron star binary mergers.

AI.tldr: The paper explores a model of Mesogenesis to generate the baryon asymmetry of the Universe through decays of B mesons, constrained by existing data but potentially modified by interactions with an ultralight scalar and thermal effects from muons in the early Universe.
AI.motivation: To investigate the potential of Mesogenesis as a mechanism for baryon asymmetry generation using Standard Model CP violation, despite constraints from experimental data on B mesons.
AI.method: The study examines the role of an ultralight scalar field that interacts with the Standard Model leptons and the dark sector, focusing on how early thermal conditions involving muons can alter the effective mass of dark fermions and enhance B meson decays.
AI.result: The proposed model shows that the dominant decay channel via dark fermions occurs in the early Universe, where muon density is high, and later becomes suppressed, aligning with observational flavor data and existing experimental limits.
AI.conclusion: The model offers a viable framework for exploring baryon asymmetry through Mesogenesis, with implications for future experimental searches for associated heavy bosons and potential signals in flavor physics and astrophysical events.

title: Geometric-Phase (Pancharatnam-Berry) Correction for Time-Bin Photonic Qudits: A Calibration and Feed-Forward Algorithm
comment: 14 pages, 5 figures. Versioned code and numerical routines available at https://github.com/97RyanW/Geometric-Phase-Correction and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19349233
summary: We develop a geometric-phase framework for time-bin photonic qudits and propose a practical calibration and feed-forward algorithm for separating and compensating geometric (Pancharatnam-Berry), dynamical, and technical phase contributions. Working directly in the time-bin basis, we use a parallel-transport gauge so that geometric phases appear as experimentally identifiable interferometric offsets, while all phase contributions enter a bin-resolved diagonal transformation. We model state preparation by cascaded unbalanced Mach-Zehnder interferometers and give closed-form amplitudes for arbitrary splitting ratios and phases, noting that single-port monitoring requires post-selection and renormalization. We then give an interferometric tomography recipe based on adjacent-bin scans, with a Fourier-basis cross-check, and a multi-mode numerical case study that separates total, dynamical, and geometric phases and demonstrates feed-forward compensation. The protocol uses standard components, including tunable UMZIs, phase shifters or EOMs, and single-photon detectors, together with routine phase sweeps. It is intended for small to moderate dimensions, approximately d up to 10, and provides a scalable route toward phase-stable high-dimensional temporal encoding for quantum communication and photonic processing.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a framework for handling geometric phases in time-bin photonic qudits, including a calibration algorithm to differentiate various phase contributions, with practical applications for quantum communication.
AI.motivation: To address the challenges associated with phase contributions in time-bin photonic qudits and improve the stability and performance in high-dimensional quantum systems.
AI.method: Development of a geometric-phase framework employing a parallel-transport gauge, modeling with unbalanced Mach-Zehnder interferometers, and implementing interferometric tomography.
AI.result: Successful separation and compensation of total, dynamical, and geometric phases through a feed-forward protocol, validated by numerical simulations and practical experimental setups.
AI.conclusion: Offers a practical and scalable approach for high-dimensional temporal encoding in quantum communication using standard optical components.

title: Observation of a Doubly-strange Hyperon $Ξ(1720)$ in $J/ψ\rightarrow{}K^{-}Σ^0\barΞ^{+}+c.c.$
summary: Based on a sample of $(10087 \pm 44) \times 10^6$ $J/ψ$ events collected with the BESIII detector at BEPCII, we report the first observation of the decay $J/ψ\rightarrow K^- Σ^0 \barΞ^++c.c.$. A partial wave analysis is performed to investigate the involved excited states. In addition to the well-established $Ξ(1690)$, a new doubly-strange hyperon $Ξ(1720) $ is observed decaying to $K^- Σ^0$ with a mass of $1721.0 \pm 5.2_{\rm stat.} \pm 3.4_{\rm syst.} ~{\rm MeV}/c^2$ and a width of $31.3 \pm 18.3_{\rm stat.} \pm 15.4_{\rm syst.} ~{\rm MeV}$, with a statistical significance exceeding $10σ$. The spin-parity hypothesis testing across various quantum number configurations reveals that the spin-parity of $Ξ(1720)$ favors $J^P = {\frac{3}{2}}^+$. Furthermore, the branching fraction of $J/ψ\rightarrow K^- Σ^0 \barΞ^++c.c.$ is determined to be $(2.68 \pm 0.04_{\rm stat.} \pm 0.17_{\rm syst.}) \times 10^{-5}$.

AI.motivation: To investigate excited states involved in the decay $J/ψightarrow K^- Σ^0  arΞ^++c.c.$ using a large dataset of $J/ψ$ events.
AI.method: Partial wave analysis of the decay events collected by the BESIII detector to identify and characterize excited states, including mass and width measurements of the new hyperon $Ξ(1720)$.
AI.result: Observation of a new hyperon $Ξ(1720)$ with mass $1721.0 	ext{ MeV}/c^2$ and a width of $31.3 	ext{ MeV}$, with a statistical significance exceeding $10σ$; branching fraction determined to be $(2.68 	imes 10^{-5})$.

title: Gaseous forms of $^{76}$Ge, $^{82}$Se, $^{96}$Zr, $^{100}$Mo, $^{124}$Sn, and $^{130}$Te: new avenues to future $0νββ$ time projection chambers
summary: Searches for neutrinoless double beta decay are growing larger, with tonne-scale targets in several nuclides still far from exhausting the discovery space. What's beyond ton scale? Time projection chambers (TPCs) are one option for building large (100~T or kiloton-scale) instruments, but filling them with the familiar $^{136}$Xe for a $0νββ$ search is a problem: xenon is a scarce element whose atmospheric-extraction supply chain is small and hard to grow. If future $0νββ$ searches wish to exploit TPCs' known hardware scalability, we need to fill them with non-xenon target materials. Of particular value would be a TPC that can drift electrons, rather than ions, letting us use mature readout schemes which require gas gain. In this paper, we identify a set of previously-unappreciated, affordable gases which are likely to be electropositive, allowing electron drift and gain in gas-phase TPCs sensitive to $0νββ$ with the help of track-topology background rejection. We identify candidate $^{76}$Ge, $^{82}$Se, $^{96}$Zr, $^{100}$Mo, $^{124}$Sn, and $^{130}$Te compounds suitable for gas-phase electron-drift TPCs; some may be suitable for liquid-phase TPCs as well. Using a figure-of-merit that emphasizes the need for track topology for background rejection, we argue that 100~T and kiloton-scale gas TPCs are realistic without unprecedented underground infrastructure.

AI.tldr: This paper explores alternatives to xenon for large-scale neutrinoless double beta decay (0νββ) searches by identifying affordable electropositive gases suitable for electron-drift time projection chambers (TPCs).
AI.motivation: To address the scarcity of xenon for large-scale 0νββ searches, the paper seeks non-xenon materials for TPCs, emphasizing the need for scalability in the search for neutrinoless double beta decay.
AI.method: The paper identifies and evaluates a range of affordable gases that allow for electron drift and gain in gas-phase TPCs, focusing on their suitability for detecting 0νββ events with background rejection based on track topology.
AI.result: Several compounds, including $^{76}$Ge, $^{82}$Se, $^{96}$Zr, $^{100}$Mo, $^{124}$Sn, and $^{130}$Te, are identified as potential candidates for TPCs, with certain gases also viable for liquid-phase systems.
AI.conclusion: The study concludes that large-scale (100 T to kiloton) gas TPCs are feasible without needing unprecedented underground infrastructure, enhancing the search for 0νββ decays.

title: Unveiling the dynamics of the ultra-fast outflow in IRAS 13224-3809 with X-ray spectroscopy
comment: Accepted to be published in Astronomy and Astrophysics
summary: IRAS 13224-3809 is one of the most intensively studied narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies, with a rich literature reporting diverse and sometimes contrasting interpretations of its complex X-ray spectra and variability. Notably, a fast and variable ultra-fast outflow (UFO) was discovered in this source, sparking debate over its nature and driving mechanisms. Motivated by these open questions, we present a systematic, time- and flux-resolved reanalysis of the full 2016 XMM-Newton (1.5 Ms) and NuSTAR (500 ks) datasets, employing careful background treatment and equal-count spectral selections. We uniformly apply three spectral models, including photo-ionized absorption, broad emission, and relativistic reflection, to all intervals. We unambiguously confirm the presence of a strong, variable outflow with velocities exceeding 0.2$c$, and find that models including absorption consistently reveal robust physical trends: a velocity-luminosity correlation of the UFO, persistently large line widths, and no compelling equivalent-width-flux anti-correlation. When emission or reflection components are included, the significance of the absorption features decreases, but significant UFO detections remain in most intervals. We also report clear evidence for rapid acceleration of the wind in response to X-ray flares, with the outflow carrying momentum and kinetic power sufficient to drive an efficient AGN feedback. The observed rapid response favors magnetic driving, analogous to coronal mass ejections, over radiative acceleration. Our results reconcile contrasting previous claims and underline the need for high-resolution spectroscopy to resolve the wind substructure. The observed UFO variability and structure are consistent with a multiphase, clumpy wind produced by thermal and hydrodynamic instabilities, with magnetic reconnection providing the rapid acceleration mechanism.

AI.tldr: This paper reanalyzes X-ray data of IRAS 13224-3809, confirming a strong ultra-fast outflow (UFO) with significant variability and acceleration linked to ACN feedback mechanisms.
AI.motivation: To address open questions regarding the nature and driving mechanisms of the UFO in IRAS 13224-3809.
AI.method: Systematic reanalysis of 2016 XMM-Newton and NuSTAR datasets using three spectral models, applying careful background treatment and uniform spectral selections.
AI.result: Confirmed strong, variable outflow with velocities >0.2$c$, revealing a velocity-luminosity correlation and evidence for wind acceleration in response to X-ray flares.
AI.conclusion: Findings reconcile previous conflicting interpretations and suggest a multiphase, clumpy wind driven by magnetic reconnection.

title: Rydberg states of muonic helium in quantum electrodynamics
summary: The variational method is used to study the energy levels of muonic helium $(μ^{-} \, e^{-} \, He)$ with an electron in the ground state and a muon in an excited state with principal and orbital quantum numbers $n \sim l+1 \sim 14$. The variational wave functions are chosen in the Gaussian form. The matrix elements of the Hamiltonian in the nonrelativistic approximation, as well as corrections for the vacuum polarization and relativism, are calculated analytically. A series of energies of the Rydberg muon states is obtained, which can be studied experimentally.

AI.tldr: This paper employs the variational method to analyze energy levels in muonic helium, achieving a series of Rydberg muon states that can be experimentally measured.
AI.motivation: The study aims to deepen the understanding of muonic helium, particularly its excited states using a variational approach.
AI.method: The variational method is applied, utilizing Gaussian wave functions for calculation of Hamiltonian matrix elements in a nonrelativistic framework while accounting for vacuum polarization and relativistic effects.
AI.result: A series of energy levels for Rydberg muon states has been derived, with specific quantum numbers identified that highlight the interaction of muon and electron in helium.
AI.conclusion: The findings provide valuable energy state information for experimental investigation of muonic helium.

title: Congestion-free routing on quantum chips
summary: Limited connectivity makes nonlocal quantum gates expensive on near-neighbor hardware, where compilation typically relies on SWAP transport, inheriting both depth overhead and path congestion. We present a swap-free routing framework in which higher levels of a qudit act as orthogonal spectral buses that transport control information without moving the computational state. We show that exact congestion relief in nearest-neighbor architectures requires local Hilbert-space expansion. In this model, a nonlocal operation over a path of length $L$ requires $2L+1$ logical routing primitives, compared to the $3L$ baseline. Overlapping routes remain distinguishable through bus labels encoded in the same physical qudits. This routing algebra extends to Boolean fan-in at a common target: multiple controls arriving on distinct buses trigger a local unitary based on an arbitrary Boolean function of bus digits, yielding multi-control operations of depth $2L + D_g + O(1)$ for fan-in size $K$ and target-synthesis cost $D_g$. We prove decodability, reversibility, and correctness for CNOT and Boolean fan-in, along with a state-count lower bound $d \geq 2^{K+1}$ for exact overlap routing. Cirq simulations confirm single-control correctness and zero crosstalk. Compiler-level benchmarks on QFT, QAOA, and mirror-interaction circuits verify the predicted congestion law and transport reduction. Noisy QuTiP simulations show that the architectural advantage depends on higher-level coherence and speed. These results identify spectral qudit routing as a congestion-relief architecture that separates nonlocal control delivery from local target-side aggregation, providing a minimal mechanism for overcoming qubit routing limitations.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a swap-free routing framework for nonlocal quantum gates in near-neighbor quantum hardware, significantly reducing routing depth and congestion.
AI.motivation: To address overhead and congestion in compiling nonlocal quantum gates using SWAP transport in limited connectivity hardware.
AI.method: The framework employs higher-level qudit states as spectral buses to route control information without moving the computational state, requiring local Hilbert-space expansion and achieving routing with fewer logical primitives.
AI.result: The proposed model reduces the required logical routing primitives from 3L to 2L + 1 for nonlocal operations, confirming correctness and decodability for CNOT and Boolean fan-in operations through simulations and benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Spectral qudit routing effectively alleviates congestion and enhances control delivery in quantum circuits, offering a minimal solution to routing limitations in qubit architectures.

title: Improved results on Higgs boson pair production in the 4b final state
comment: Submitted to Physical Review D. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/HIG-24-010 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: Measurements of Higgs boson pair (HH) production in the four bottom quark (4b) final state are presented using proton-proton (pp) collision data at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62 fb$^{-1}$. Events in which the Higgs boson decays, H$\mathrm{t\bar{t}}$, are separately reconstructed as pairs of small-radius jets (resolved), as well as those where they are reconstructed as single large-radius jets (merged), are studied exclusively. Benefiting from new methods in trigger selection, event selection, and signal extraction, the combination of analyses in the resolved and merged topologies gives an observed (expected) upper limit on the HH signal strength, $μ_\mathrm{HH}$, of 4.4 (4.4) at 95% confidence level (CL). Compared to previously published LHC results in the 4b final state, the expected limit with an equivalent integrated luminosity is improved by more than a factor of two in the resolved topology and is better in the merged topology as well. An updated analysis of the resolved topology using 138 fb$^{-1}$ of 13 TeV pp collision data yields an observed (expected) 95% CL upper limit on $μ_\mathrm{HH}$ of 10.0 (5.9), an improvement of about 25% in the expected limit compared to the published results using the same data. Results in the 4b final state with 13 and 13.6 TeV are combined, resulting in an observed (expected) 95% CL upper limit on $μ_\mathrm{HH}$ of 4.7 (2.8). The allowed ranges for the Higgs boson trilinear self-coupling and quartic coupling between two Higgs bosons and two vector bosons are also reported. These are the most stringent constraints achieved in the 4b final state to date.

AI.tldr: The paper reports improved upper limits on Higgs boson pair production in the 4b final state using CMS data, with significant enhancements in analysis methods.
AI.motivation: To measure Higgs boson pair production (HH) in the four bottom quark (4b) final state and constrain associated couplings.
AI.method: Analysis of pp collision data at 13.6 TeV with integrated luminosity of 62 fb$^{-1}$, including both resolved and merged topologies.
AI.result: Observed (expected) upper limit on HH signal strength is 4.4 (4.4) at 95% CL, improved by more than a factor of two in resolved topology compared to prior results.
AI.conclusion: These results provide the most stringent constraints on Higgs boson couplings in the 4b final state to date.

title: Finding Strongly Lensed Supernovae from Blended Light Curves
summary: We present a model-independent, photometry-only framework for identifying strongly lensed supernovae when multiple images are unresolved and blended into a single point source. Building on the simulation-based methodology of Bag et al. (2021), we apply this approach to real Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) data using a validation sample of spectroscopically confirmed Type Ia supernovae. The method models the observed flux as a superposition of two time-shifted components, and Bayesian inference is used to estimate the relative scaling and time delay. Applying this framework to 445 well-converged supernovae, we find that only a single object satisfies the selection criteria when adopting a conservative threshold of $Δt \ge 12$ days, corresponding to a false positive fraction of $1/445 \approx 0.22\%$. A laxer threshold of $Δt \ge 10$ days yields fourteen objects, for a false positive fraction of $3.15\%$. The method provides a scalable and model-independent first-stage filter for identifying lens-like candidates in large time-domain surveys such as the Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST).

AI.tldr: A new method for detecting strongly lensed supernovae in blended images is presented, validated using ZTF data. It estimates time delays and scaling through Bayesian analysis, yielding minimal false positives.
AI.motivation: To effectively identify strongly lensed supernovae in situations where multiple images blend into a single source, enhancing data analysis from large surveys.
AI.method: The framework uses a superposition model of two time-shifted components, applying Bayesian inference to assess relative scaling and time delays based on ZTF data.
AI.result: Out of 445 supernovae, one meets the conservative selection criteria (Δt ≥ 12 days) and 14 under laxer criteria (Δt ≥ 10 days), with low false positive rates of 0.22% and 3.15% respectively.
AI.conclusion: This method provides a scalable and model-independent approach for the preliminary filtering of lens-like candidates in extensive time-domain surveys.

title: Optical effects in Gaseous Electron Multipliers (GEMs)
comment: Submitted to Nuclear Instruments and Methods A, 16 pages, 12 figures
summary: Optical time projection chambers (OTPCs) are well suited for applications that require the highest spatial resolution for particle track reconstruction. The MIGDAL experiment uses a glass GEM-based OTPC and observes a systematic excess in both the intensity and width of particle tracks in its optical readout, when compared with charge readout simulations. One hypothesis is that scintillation light produced inside a GEM hole during the avalanche propagates through the GEM substrate and exits neighboring holes. We present lab measurements testing this hypothesized optical broadening effect in three types of GEM substrates: glass, ceramic, and FR4. Our observations quantify this optical broadening and demonstrate it to be strongest in glass GEMs. Additionally, we use Geant4 simulations to both reproduce our observations and quantify optical broadening effects in realistic charge avalanches. Applying our glass GEM effects to simulated particle tracks yields increases of track intensity and widths by up to around 26% and 31%, respectively. This may explain the larger than expected intensity and track widths observed in the MIGDAL OTPC and is expected to be an observed effect in all GEM-based OTPCs.

AI.tldr: This study investigates the optical broadening effect observed in the MIGDAL experiment using glass GEM-based OTPCs, demonstrating that scintillation light from avalanches causes increased track intensity and width compared to simulations.
AI.motivation: To understand the discrepancies in track intensity and width observed in the MIGDAL experiment when comparing optical readout with charge readout simulations.
AI.method: Lab measurements were conducted on three types of GEM substrates (glass, ceramic, and FR4) to quantify optical broadening caused by scintillation light. Geant4 simulations were used to reproduce and quantify these effects in realistic charge avalanches.
AI.result: The study found that optical broadening was strongest in glass GEMs, leading to increases in track intensity and widths by up to roughly 26% and 31% in simulations.
AI.conclusion: The optical broadening effect may account for the larger tracking parameters observed in the MIGDAL OTPC, suggesting it is a general phenomenon in all GEM-based OTPCs.

title: Optimised Inference of Quantum Phenomena in High-Energy Collider Experiments
summary: Entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon of quantum theory, has recently been observed in processes in high-energy physics. This opens new avenues for probing quantum effects in relativistic regimes, but also poses conceptual and technical challenges. We develop a general framework based on shadow tomography techniques for characterising spin-spin correlations in collider experiments. This improves the analysis of spin-spin entanglement, where relativistic motion couples spin and momentum and the momenta of the investigated particles are not under experimental control. As a proof of concept we illustrate the application of our formalism to top quark pair production at the Large Hadron Collider at CERN. The framework, however, is general and flexible and can be readily applied to more complex final states and systems with more particles.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a framework for analyzing spin-spin entanglement in high-energy physics, particularly in collider experiments, using shadow tomography techniques.
AI.motivation: To address the conceptual and technical challenges in characterizing quantum effects in relativistic physics.
AI.method: A general framework based on shadow tomography is developed to analyze spin-spin correlations in collider experiments, accommodating the coupling of spin and momentum in relativistic conditions.
AI.result: Application of the framework to top quark pair production at the Large Hadron Collider demonstrates its effectiveness; the approach is adaptable to more complex scenarios.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework is versatile and can enhance the analysis of quantum entanglement in various particle interactions.

title: Ground state energy of particle in space with minimal length and momentum
summary: In this article, we derive a rigorous lower bound on the ground-state energy for a class of one-dimensional quantum systems in deformed space with minimal coordinate and momentum uncertainties, representing the absolute minimum energy that is physically attainable. We consider a harmonic oscillator in such a space and calculate its ground state energy. We generalized the problem to an arbitrary potential, deriving an equation for the coordinate uncertainty corresponding to the minimal energy, which can be solved numerically. Using a linear approximation in the deformation parameters, we obtained a general expression for the ground-state energy. We determined the domain of existence of solutions for the anharmonic oscillator potential with respect to the deformation parameters.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a method to determine a lower bound on the ground-state energy of one-dimensional quantum systems in deformed space with uncertainties, focusing on both harmonic and anharmonic oscillator potentials.
AI.motivation: To establish a rigorous lower bound for the ground-state energy in quantum systems facing minimal uncertainties in coordinates and momenta.
AI.method: The authors derive a lower bound on ground-state energy, analyze a harmonic oscillator case, generalize to arbitrary potentials, and solve for coordinate uncertainty numerically while employing a linear approximation for deformation parameters.
AI.result: A general expression for ground-state energy is formulated, and the existence domains for solutions in the context of anharmonic oscillator potentials are identified based on deformation parameters.
AI.conclusion: The findings provide essential insights into the behavior of quantum systems under deformed conditions, revealing how uncertainties impact ground-state energy.

title: Energy efficiency of a GPU-based computing system for High Energy Physics experiments
comment: Submitting to Frontiers in Physics - High-Energy and Astroparticle Physics
summary: In this paper we introduce the energy efficiency as a new metric for evaluating both hardware platforms based on Graphic Processor Units (GPU), and algorithm optimisations at High Energy Physics (HEP) experiments. We develop a method to compute the energy efficiency for the case of the first high level trigger (HLT1) of the LHCb experiment, relating the throughput with GPU specifications such as the number of cores, clock frequency, memory bandwidth and thermal design power. The model can be extended to other HEP experiments to make decisions and reach sustainable computing ecosystems.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces energy efficiency as a metric for evaluating GPU hardware and algorithms in High Energy Physics experiments, specifically focusing on the LHCb experiment.
AI.motivation: The need for sustainable computing in High Energy Physics necessitates new metrics for performance evaluation, particularly in the context of energy consumption.
AI.method: The authors develop a method to compute energy efficiency by relating throughput to GPU specifications like core count, clock frequency, memory bandwidth, and thermal design power.
AI.result: The model successfully quantifies energy efficiency for the first high-level trigger of the LHCb experiment and demonstrates potential adaptability to other HEP experiments.
AI.conclusion: The proposed model can support decision-making for achieving more sustainable computing ecosystems in High Energy Physics.

title: An Extended Evaluation Split for DeepSpaceYoloDataset
summary: Recent technological advances in astronomy, particularly the growing popularity of smart telescopes for the general public, make it possible to develop highly effective detection solutions that are accessible to a wide audience, rather than being reserved for major scientific observatories. Published in 2023, DeepSpaceYoloDataset is a collection of annotated images created to train YOLO-based models for detecting Deep Sky Objects, particularly suited for Electronically Assisted Astronomy. In this paper, we present an update to DeepSpaceYoloDataset with the addition of a new split, test2026, designed to evaluate detection models with a greater diversity of images.

AI.tldr: The paper updates the DeepSpaceYoloDataset to enhance the detection of Deep Sky Objects using YOLO models, adding a new test set for improved model evaluation.
AI.motivation: To democratize astronomy through effective detection solutions accessible via smart telescopes, enhancing public engagement.
AI.method: Updated the DeepSpaceYoloDataset with a newly added test split, test2026, to train and evaluate YOLO models for detecting Deep Sky Objects.
AI.result: The inclusion of the test2026 split aims to provide a more diverse testing environment for detection models, improving their accuracy and effectiveness.
AI.conclusion: The updated dataset facilitates better training and assessment of YOLO-based models, supporting advancements in Electronically Assisted Astronomy.

title: Optimisation of a silicon-tungsten electromagnetic calorimeter energy response to photons
summary: An innovative path for the detectors at future colliders to achieve higher performances is to use a Particle Flow approach, which requires highly granular calorimeters to image individual showers. The silicon-tungsten electromagnetic calorimeter (SiW-ECAL) aims at fulfilling all the expected physical and technical requirements. SiW-ECAL has been developed by the CALICE and ILD collaborations for more than two decades and is now reaching maturity, for linear machines. However, with the tendency towards circular machines, the progress of electronics and the rapid advancement of machine learning (ML) techniques, the SiW-ECAL design needs to be reoptimised to enhance its performance. This study develops ML-based reconstruction approaches for SiW-ECAL, achieving an approximate 20% improvement in energy resolution in the low-energy range and effectively correcting energy leakage in the high-energy range. Subsequently, the SiW-ECAL design is reoptimized based on this method.

AI.tldr: The study presents ML-based optimizations for the SiW-ECAL, enhancing energy resolution by 20%, and addresses design reoptimizations for future collider applications.
AI.motivation: The necessity for improved detector performance at future colliders and adaptability for circular machines drive the optimization of the SiW-ECAL.
AI.method: The study employs machine learning techniques to reconstruct particle energy measurements in the SiW-ECAL, leading to significant enhancements in both low and high-energy performance.
AI.result: Achieved a 20% improvement in energy resolution at low energies and corrected energy leakage at high energies through ML-based methods.
AI.conclusion: The approach not only improves the SiW-ECAL's performance but also suggests necessary design modifications for evolving collider technologies.

title: Planar master integrals for two-loop NLO electroweak light-fermion contributions to $g g \rightarrow Z H$
summary: For the two-loop next-to-leading-order electroweak (NLO EW) corrections to $gg \rightarrow ZH$, the light-fermion contributions can be classified into eight distinct topologies. Using the canonical differential-equations method, we perform an analytic computation of the master integrals (MIs) associated with the four planar topologies. Canonical bases are constructed using the Magnus-expansion method, and the resulting alphabets consist of algebraic symbol letters involving nontrivial radicals. We develop a systematic framework for identifying the radical structures of the canonical MIs, enabling their organization into suitable subsystems and, whenever possible, their representation in terms of Goncharov polylogarithms (GPLs) up to $\mathcal{O}(ε^4)$. Only a few MIs at $\mathcal{O}(ε^3)$ and $\mathcal{O}(ε^4)$ are instead represented as one-fold integrals over GPLs, due to the presence of nested square roots that obstruct the simultaneous rationalization of all radicals.

AI.tldr: This paper details the analytic computation of master integrals for electroweak corrections to a specific particle interaction using a systematic approach to radical structures.
AI.motivation: To enhance the understanding of two-loop NLO EW corrections in particle physics, specifically for the process $gg ightarrow ZH$.
AI.method: Utilizes the canonical differential-equations method for computing master integrals of planar topologies and applies the Magnus-expansion method for constructing canonical bases.
AI.result: Identified radical structures of the master integrals and organized them into subsystems, with several integrals expressed as one-fold integrals over Goncharov polylogarithms due to complexity in radical forms.
AI.conclusion: The framework developed aids in managing the complexity of master integrals which involve nontrivial radicals, contributing to the computation of NLO EW corrections.

title: Efficient mapping of multi-constraint satisfaction problems to Rydberg platforms
summary: We present a hardware-native gadget framework for solving constraint satisfaction problems on Rydberg quantum computing architectures. Our approach introduces a compact $xor_1$ gadget that enforces exactly-one constraints, ubiquitous in combinatorial optimization, directly through geometric embedding and blockade interactions. A key advantage of the $xor_1$ gadget is its fixed, problem-size-independent detuning requirements: enforcing constraints through blockade interactions eliminates the need for large penalty terms, thereby substantially reducing the detuning range compared to Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) formulations and improving experimental feasibility. By tailoring the construction to the geometric connectivity of Rydberg atom arrays, the framework bypasses the all-to-all physical couplings often assumed in logical encodings. This enables embeddings compatible with planar layouts and avoids highly connected arrangements. We develop scalable implementations that reduce atom count and connectivity overhead while avoiding extensive classical preprocessing, making them compatible with near-term neutral-atom hardware. As illustrations, we apply our framework to the gate-assignment and $N$-queens problems, highlighting its practicality, resource efficiency, and hardware compatibility. In these examples, we observe reductions in detuning range of up to $99\%$ and savings in atom count and connectivity overhead of up to $54\%$ compared to the QUBO method. These results establish a route toward implementing large-scale combinatorial optimization on Rydberg platforms beyond the limits of existing encodings.

AI.tldr: A framework is introduced for solving constraint satisfaction problems on Rydberg quantum architectures using a new $xor_1$ gadget, which improves efficiency by reducing detuning requirements and resource overhead compared to traditional methods.
AI.motivation: To enhance the implementation of combinatorial optimization problems on Rydberg quantum computers, addressing the limitations of existing encodings and detuning constraints.
AI.method: Introducing a compact $xor_1$ gadget that enforces exactly-one constraints via geometric embedding and blockade interactions, tailored to the geometric connectivity of Rydberg atom arrays.
AI.result: Achieved reductions in detuning range by up to 99% and atom count/connectivity overhead by up to 54% compared to QUBO formulations.
AI.conclusion: This framework paves the way for scalable combinatorial optimization on Rydberg platforms, significantly enhancing their practicality and efficiency.

title: Search for light charged Higgs bosons decaying to charm and strange quarks in $\mathrm{t\bar{t}}$ events in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
comment: Submitted to the Journal of High Energy Physics. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/B2G-23-003 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: A search is presented for a light charged Higgs boson H$^\pm$ in top quark pair production ($\mathrm{t\bar{t}}$), where one of the top quarks decays to an H$^\pm$ and a bottom quark, while the other decays to a W$^\mp$ boson and a bottom quark. The H$^\pm$ is assumed to decay into a charm and a strange quark, whereas the W$^\mp$ boson decays into a charged lepton (electron or muon) and a neutrino. Results are reported based on proton-proton collision data at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$. The analysis probes H$^\pm$ masses in the range 40 to 160 GeV using the invariant mass spectrum of the two light jets, where light jets are defined as jets that do not satisfy the bottom quark tagging requirement. The observed yield is found to be consistent with standard model predictions. Upper limits are set on the branching fraction $\mathcal{B}$(t $\to$ H$^\pm$ b), with values in the range of 0.07$-$1.12% at 95% confidence level, under the assumption that $\mathcal{B}$(H$^\pm$ $\to$ cs) = 100%. These are the first direct limits on charged Higgs bosons produced in top quark decays for masses between 40 and 50 GeV, and the most stringent limits to date in the 70$-$110 GeV range.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a search for light charged Higgs bosons (H$^	imes$) in top quark pair production, analyzing decay channels and setting upper limits on branching fractions based on proton-proton collision data.
AI.motivation: To explore the existence of light charged Higgs bosons in top quark decays, testing predictions beyond the Standard Model.
AI.method: The analysis utilizes proton-proton collision data at 13 TeV, focusing on invariant mass spectra of jets from specific decay pathways of top quarks.
AI.result: The observed yields align with Standard Model predictions, establishing upper limits on the branching fraction of t $	o$ H$^	imes$ b in the 40-160 GeV mass range.
AI.conclusion: These results represent the first direct limits on charged Higgs bosons from top quark decays for 40-50 GeV and provide the most stringent limits for the 70-110 GeV mass range.

title: Radio signal generation in milliseconds: enabling multi-parameter reconstruction of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays
comment: Presented at the 60th Rencontres de Moriond (Moriond 2026). 4 pages, 2 figures
summary: In recent years, radio detection of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs), with energies above $10^{18}$ eV, has become an established technique. The radio emissions can be simulated with high accuracy using Monte Carlo codes such as ZHAireS and CoREAS. These simulations are essential but are computationally intensive. In this work, we present a machine-learning-based emulator that reproduces radio signal simulations with high accuracy in milliseconds rather than hours. Primary particle properties can then be reconstructed by comparing measured signals to emulated traces using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo approach. Using ZHAireS simulations carried out over the GRANDProto300 experiment layout, the method achieves an 8.9\% resolution on electromagnetic energy and a 0.08° angular resolution, matching state-of-the-art reconstruction performance. Finally, we apply the method on real data, successfully reconstructing cosmic-ray candidates detected by the GP300 prototype.

AI.tldr: A machine-learning emulator for the radio detection of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays allows rapid and accurate simulations, achieving state-of-the-art reconstruction of cosmic-ray properties.
AI.motivation: To address the computational intensity of simulating radio emissions from ultra-high-energy cosmic rays, enhancing efficiency while preserving accuracy.
AI.method: A machine-learning emulator is developed to replicate simulations from Monte Carlo codes, paired with a Markov Chain Monte Carlo approach for reconstructing primary particle properties.
AI.result: Achieved 8.9% resolution on electromagnetic energy and 0.08° angular resolution, successfully applied to real data with cosmic-ray candidate detection.
AI.conclusion: The emulator demonstrates a significant improvement in simulation speed and accuracy, facilitating effective analysis of cosmic rays in experimental setups.

title: Macroscopic photon counting beating the Poisson noise limit
summary: Photon counting is a cornerstone of quantum optics. Here, we demonstrate precisely counting from 0 to over 9000 photons, beating the Poisson noise limit by at least $4.1~\mathrm{dB}$ across this range. We achieve sub-single-photon precision up to 276 photons per pulse. To do so, we multiplex eight intrinsically photon-number-resolving superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors across 128 temporal modes. We use a model-informed characterization of each of the 1024 detection bins, for optimal precision. We perform quantum detector tomography to reconstruct the positive operator valued measures (POVMs) of the complete device, which consists of $1.38\cdot10^8$ matrix elements. At the repetition rate of our experiment of $80~\mathrm{kHz}$, we can precisely count photons corresponding to an optical power of approximately $71~\mathrm{pW}$, bridging the gap from single-photon measurements to high-sensitivity optical power meters. A photon-number-resolving detector of this size, and the tools used to analyze it, will become increasingly important to characterize large quantum states, as well as tasks in precision metrology and optical power standards.

AI.tldr: Demonstrated precise photon counting from 0 to 9000 photons with sub-single-photon precision, surpassing Poisson noise limits by 4.1 dB. Utilized multiplexing of superconducting nanowire detectors and characterized detection bins for optimal precision.
AI.motivation: To improve photon counting precision beyond Poisson noise limits, facilitating advancements in quantum optics and high-sensitivity measurements.
AI.method: Multiplexed eight photon-number-resolving superconducting nanowire detectors over 128 temporal modes and characterized detection bins through a model-informed approach and quantum detector tomography.
AI.result: Achieved precise counting up to 9000 photons with 4.1 dB improvement over Poisson noise, and sub-single-photon precision for pulses of up to 276 photons.
AI.conclusion: This advanced photon-number-resolving detector will enhance characterization of large quantum states and improve precision metrology and optical power standards.

title: Multi-messenger emission from choked jets in collapsar
comment: Contribution to the 2026 Very High Energy Phenomena in the Universe session of the 60th Rencontres de Moriond
summary: The death of massive stars produces central accreting compact objects and sometimes relativistic jets. Not all jets escape the stellar envelope: unsuccessful, or choked, jets dissipate their energy into a pressurized cocoon, which expands and may break out as a mildly relativistic outflow. We investigate the plasma physics of collapsing massive stars hosting choked jets through relativistic, non-resistive magnetohydrodynamical simulations. We delineate the parameter space for jet choking and quantify the acceleration rate and efficiency of charged particles at strong shocks, which are potential sources of high-energy neutrinos and electromagnetic transients. Our study focuses on blue and red supergiant progenitors, both promising candidates for jet choking.

AI.tldr: The study explores the physics of choked jets in collapsing massive stars, focusing on their formation and implications for high-energy phenomena.
AI.motivation: To understand the mechanisms behind choked jets in massive stars and their impact on high-energy astrophysical processes.
AI.method: The authors used relativistic, non-resistive magnetohydrodynamical simulations to analyze the plasma physics in collapsing massive stars.
AI.result: The study identifies the parameter space for jet choking and quantifies the acceleration of charged particles in strong shocks.
AI.conclusion: Choked jets in blue and red supergiant progenitors may play a crucial role in producing high-energy neutrinos and electromagnetic transients.

title: Electroweak Baryogenesis from Collapsing Domain Walls
summary: We propose a novel mechanism for electroweak baryogenesis in which collapsing domain walls formed by an axion-like field replace the bubble walls in a strong first-order electroweak phase transition. The axion-like particle coupling to the Higgs mass term allows domain walls to separate regions with distinct electroweak phases, while the electroweak crossover induces a potential-energy bias that triggers their collapse. The directed wall motion, through the axion-like particle coupling to the electroweak topological term, acts as an effective baryon chemical potential and generates an asymmetry via electroweak sphaleron processes. We show that the observed baryon asymmetry can be obtained from either late-time entropy injection or sphaleron suppression in a weakly broken electroweak domain. The wall collapse also produces a stochastic gravitational-wave background with features distinct from standard electroweak-scale first-order-transition spectra.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a new mechanism for electroweak baryogenesis using collapsing domain walls formed by an axion-like field, which creates an asymmetry through electroweak processes and leads to unique gravitational-wave signatures.
AI.motivation: To explore alternative mechanisms for achieving baryon asymmetry in the universe during the electroweak phase transition, using axion-like fields and their interactions.
AI.method: The authors propose the use of collapsing domain walls resulting from an axion-like field to separate different electroweak phases, where the collapse triggers baryogenesis through effective chemical potential and sphaleron processes.
AI.result: The proposed mechanism can yield the observed baryon asymmetry either through late-time entropy injection or sphaleron suppression, and leads to the generation of a distinctive gravitational-wave background.
AI.conclusion: This novel approach to baryogenesis not only accounts for the baryon asymmetry but also offers a unique gravitational-wave emission profile that differs from standard models.

title: Some applications of Choi polynomials of linear maps
summary: This paper investigates the properties of Choi polynomials and their fundamental role in the theory of positive linear maps between matrix algebras. By focusing on Hermitian symmetric biquadratic forms, we establish a connection between the positivity of these forms and the structure of positive maps. We specifically explore the construction of indecomposable positive maps in matrix algebras, and their application as entanglement witnesses. Our analysis extends to the detection of Positive Partial Transpose (PPT) entangled states and the classification of edge PPT states in $M_m(\mathbb{C}) \otimes M_n(\mathbb{C})$. Our results provide a refined framework for identifying non-separable states that escape the standard PPT criterion, contributing to the broader understanding of entanglement distillation and quantum information theory.

AI.tldr: The paper explores Choi polynomials, emphasizing their significance in positive linear maps in matrix algebras. It highlights a link between Hermitian symmetric biquadratic forms and positive maps.
AI.motivation: To enhance the understanding of positive linear maps and their implications in quantum information theory, particularly regarding entanglement.
AI.method: The study examines Hermitian symmetric biquadratic forms, investigates indecomposable positive maps, and analyzes their role in detecting PPT entangled states.
AI.result: The paper establishes connections between the positivity of forms and positive maps, leading to a refined framework for identifying non-separable states beyond the PPT criterion.
AI.conclusion: This work contributes to the theory of quantum entanglement and provides insights into entanglement distillation and the classification of edge PPT states.

title: The DAMSA Experiment
comment: 35 pages, 26 figures. arXiv admin note: substantial text overlap with arXiv:2601.15255
summary: DAMSA (DArk Messenger Searches at an Accelerator) is a novel short-baseline accelerator/beam dump experiment aimed at probing short-lived physics processes, including searches for evidence of a dark sector of particle physics and well-motivated rare Standard Model signals. Motivated by open questions in neutrino physics and the absence of conclusive evidence for conventional weakly interacting massive particles, DAMSA targets MeV-to-sub-GeV dark-sector messengers with feeble couplings that can be produced in abundance at a beam dump/target. By employing an ultra-short baseline, DAMSA is uniquely positioned to overcome the beam-dump "ceiling" that limits sensitivity to fast decaying particles in longer-baseline experiments. The conceptual design emphasizes a beam-dump production scheme combined with a compact detector optimized for rare decays while mitigating intense neutron-induced backgrounds, inherent to high-power proton beams. To validate the experimental strategy and detector technologies, the DAMSA Path-Finder (DPF) proof-of-concept experiment is also proposed, focusing on axion-like particles decaying to two photons, as the benchmark physics case and operating with 8 GeV electron beams at SLAC Linac-to-ESA (LESA) facility. Successful realization of DPF will establish the feasibility of the DAMSA approach, enabling a broad and powerful program to explore short-lived new physics and precision Standard Model processes in a previously inaccessible regime. This paper outlines the technical details of DAMSA's physics goals, key experimental challenges, and how to overcome them.

AI.tldr: DAMSA is a novel experiment aimed at probing short-lived particle physics, targeting MeV-to-sub-GeV dark-sector messengers and rare Standard Model signals, using an ultra-short baseline to enhance sensitivity.
AI.motivation: The experiment seeks to address questions in neutrino physics and the lack of evidence for weakly interacting massive particles, exploring new physics realms.
AI.method: DAMSA employs a beam-dump production scheme with a compact detector, optimized to detect rare decays and mitigate neutron-induced backgrounds, alongside a proof-of-concept experiment (DPF).
AI.result: The DPF aims to validate the DAMSA approach, focusing on axion-like particles as a benchmark, using an 8 GeV electron beam at SLAC.
AI.conclusion: The successful realization of DPF will pave the way for DAMSA's broader program, enabling exploration of new physics and precision measurements in previously inaccessible regions.

title: The Large Array Survey Telescope-Pipeline. II. Image Subtraction and Transient Detection
summary: Context. The Large Array Survey Telescope (LAST) is a wide-field visual-band survey designed to explore the variable and transient sky with high cadence. Its raw data stream is automatically processed in near real time at the observatory site, producing science-quality images, catalogs, and transient alerts. Transient alerts are then reported to the Transient Name Server (TNS). Aims. The LAST pipeline comprises two major components: (i) processing and calibration of single images followed by coaddition of $20\times20$s exposures, producing single-image and coadded-image catalogs; and (ii) subtraction of coadded images from calibrated reference images followed by transient detection. In this work we present a detailed description and validation of the second component of the pipeline. Methods. Transient detection is based on the algorithm for proper image subtraction (ZOGY). We combine ZOGY subtraction with the Translient statistic for sub-pixel motion discrimination, together with a sequence of deterministic filtering steps, to produce a clean stream of transient candidates without the use of machine learning. Results. Using commissioning data, the pipeline achieves a preliminary $5σ$ limiting magnitude of $20.3$-$20.7$mag, a single-epoch transient detection efficiency of $\sim80$%, and a purity of $\gtrsim90$% at signal-to-noise ratio of $\geq7.5σ$.

AI.tldr: The Large Array Survey Telescope (LAST) processes transient sky data in real-time, focusing on image calibration and transient detection using ZOGY algorithm without machine learning.
AI.motivation: To develop a reliable pipeline for detecting transient astronomical events with high efficiency and purity.
AI.method: Utilizes the ZOGY algorithm along with a sequence of deterministic filtering steps for image subtraction and transient identification.
AI.result: Achieves a $5σ$ limiting magnitude of $20.3$-$20.7$mag, with $	ext{~80	ext{	extperthousand}}$ transient detection efficiency and purity of $	ext{~90	ext{	extperthousand}}$ at S/N $	ext{~7.5σ}$.
AI.conclusion: The proposed transient detection pipeline provides a robust framework for identifying transient candidates in astronomical surveys.

title: Constraints on a Light Singlet Scalar from Combined Exotic Higgs Decays
comment: 20 pages, 8 figures, Accepted by Physica Scripta
summary: We investigate the phenomenology of the Standard Model extended by a real gauge-singlet scalar field, focusing on exotic Higgs decay channels. For a light scalar mass in the range \(0 < m_φ < 40\) GeV, the Higgs boson can decay to both two and three scalar final states. We derive analytical expressions for these decay rates and impose a global constraint on the model parameters by requiring that their sum does not exceed the total Standard Model Higgs boson decay width. This requirement translates into a fourth-order inequality with respect to the singlet vacuum expectation value, \(v_φ\). We demonstrate that satisfying this inequality imposes an upper bound of \(\cos θ< 0.12 - 0.13\) across the entire mass range, providing a complementary constraint to existing direct search limits. Utilizing stronger independent constraints on the mixing (e.g., \(\cos θ< 0.1\)), we then predict upper bounds on the individual exotic decay rates as a function of \(m_φ\) as \(Γ_{h \rightarrow φφ} < 0.06\) MeV and \(Γ_{h \rightarrow φφφ} < 5 \times 10^{- 6}\) MeV, respectively.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the effects of adding a real gauge-singlet scalar field to the Standard Model, particularly focusing on new decay channels for the Higgs boson. It derives conditions for the model parameters based on decay rate constraints and provides specific predictions for exotic decay rates.
AI.motivation: To examine the effects of a gauge-singlet scalar field on Higgs boson decay modes and to identify observable consequences of this extension of the Standard Model.
AI.method: Analytical expressions for exotic Higgs decay rates were derived and constraints were imposed to ensure the total decay width does not exceed that of the Standard Model. A fourth-order inequality in terms of the singlet vacuum expectation value was formulated.

title: Permutation Invariant Optimization Problems in Quantum Information Theory: A Framework for Channel Fidelity and Beyond
comment: 62 pages, 6 figures. See also the accompanying paper from today: Parentin, Bergh, Datta, Wilde: Onset of superactivation of quantum capacity
summary: Exploiting permutation invariance to reduce the exponential scaling of semidefinite programs in quantum information has emerged as a powerful computational technique. In this work, we develop a systematic framework for using this reduction via Schur-Weyl duality for optimization problems, and establish methods that allow one to work fully inside the permutation invariant subspace while performing operations such as (partially) applying channels and taking (partial) traces, or computing expressions like the quantum relative entropy. We then apply our techniques to the problem of computing efficient lower bounds on the channel fidelity over $n$ parallel uses of a quantum channel. The algorithm, which we call symmetric seesaw method, exploits permutation-invariant codes to yield improved lower bounds on the channel fidelity over $n$ uses of the depolarizing and amplitude-damping channel in the regime of tens of channel uses, and was used in [Parentin, Bergh, Datta, Wilde: Onset of superactivation of quantum capacity, arXiv: today] to demonstrate non-asymptotic superactivation of quantum capacity for $n = 17$. An implementation of our methods, aimed at being suitable for various quantum information theoretic optimization problems, is also available as an open-source Python package.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a framework using permutation invariance and Schur-Weyl duality to optimize semidefinite programs in quantum information, leading to improved algorithms for channel fidelity computation.
AI.motivation: The exponential scaling of semidefinite programs in quantum information necessitates efficient computational techniques.
AI.method: A systematic framework leveraging Schur-Weyl duality, focusing on operations within the permutation invariant subspace for tasks like applying channels and computing quantum relative entropy.
AI.result: The symmetric seesaw method yields improved lower bounds on channel fidelity for both depolarizing and amplitude-damping channels, successfully applied in a recent study on superactivation of quantum capacity.
AI.conclusion: An open-source Python package implements these methods, enhancing accessibility for quantum information theoretic optimization problems.

title: First Detection of Faraday Rotation in a Gamma-Ray Burst Afterglow: Low Polarization and High Rotation Measure in GRB 260310A Reveal Jet Magnetic Structure and Environment
comment: Submitted to ApJL, 19 pages, 7 figures, comments welcome
summary: We report the detection of linear polarization in the radio afterglow of GRB 260310A, representing the first centimeter-wavelength polarization detection of a gamma-ray burst (GRB) afterglow and the first measurement of Faraday rotation in a GRB environment. We detect linearly polarized emission across $11-25$ GHz, with a polarization fraction decreasing monotonically from $(3.18 \pm 0.18)\%$ at 25 GHz to $(0.69 \pm 0.22)\%$ at 11 GHz. Interpreting the radio data as emission from a reverse shock in a structured, relativistic jet, the observed depolarization toward lower frequencies is consistent with suppression by synchrotron self-absorption, while the low observed polarization at high frequencies relative to the theoretical maximum suggests a patchy magnetic field in the jet with a coherence scale, $θ_{\rm B}\approx10^{-2}$ rad. We identify a frequency-dependent rotation of the polarization angle consistent with Faraday rotation, with a rotation measure of ${\rm RM} = -(8300 \pm 90)~\rm{rad/m^2}$ at the GRB redshift. The magnitude of the rotation measure is consistent with propagation through a dense, magnetized environment, such as a progenitor HII region. These findings demonstrate that GRB afterglows exhibit measurable linear polarization at centimeter wavelengths, and that their polarimetric properties probe both intrinsic jet magnetization and the surrounding medium. Future multi-frequency polarimetric monitoring over timescales of days to weeks will enable detailed studies of the evolution of magnetic field structure and provide new constraints on the role of magnetic fields in GRB afterglows.

AI.tldr: This study presents the first detection of linear polarization in the radio afterglow of GRB 260310A, marking a significant advancement in understanding gamma-ray burst environments and jet properties.
AI.motivation: To investigate polarization in GRB afterglows and understand the magnetic field structure within the jets and surrounding environments.
AI.method: Analysis of radio afterglow polarization at frequencies between 11-25 GHz, measuring polarization fractions and interpreting these in terms of synchrotron self-absorption and Faraday rotation.
AI.result: Detected linear polarization that decreases with frequency and identified a rotation measure of -8300 ± 90 rad/m², suggesting a magnetized environment around the GRB.
AI.conclusion: The findings indicate that GRB afterglows have measurable polarization at centimeter wavelengths, providing insights into jet magnetization and surrounding media, with implications for future polarization studies.

title: Low mass scalars at $e^+e-$ colliders
comment: 13 pages, 9 figures; invited review contribution to proceedings of LCWS 2025, will be published in The European Physical Journal - Plus - Focus topics
summary: I briefly discuss the search for low mass scalars at Higgs factories as well as available models that render such scalars feasible, where I focus on new developments since the review presented in arXiv:2205.09687 (see also arXiv:2504.11969 for a recent update).

AI.method: The author reviews available models and developments related to low mass scalars in the context of Higgs physics.

title: Onset of superactivation of quantum capacity
comment: 64 pages, 12 figures. See also the accompanying paper from today: Bergh, Parentin: Permutation Invariant Optimization Problems in Quantum Information Theory: A Framework for Channel Fidelity and Beyond
summary: Superactivation of quantum capacity is the phenomenon whereby two quantum channels, each with zero quantum capacity, can exhibit a strictly positive capacity when used in tandem. In this work, we explore superactivation in the previously unexplored non-asymptotic regime of finitely many channel uses. We give a definition of finite-blocklength superactivation and propose numerical methods that can certify it. Then, focusing on the 50% erasure and positive-partial-transpose channels considered in the original work on superactivation, we show that as few as 17 uses of the joint channel already enable qubit transmission with a fidelity unattainable by any number of uses of either channel alone, demonstrating a strong finite-blocklength form of superactivation and opening the door to experimental demonstration.

AI.tldr: This work investigates the superactivation of quantum channels with zero capacity, demonstrating that, when used together, they can achieve a positive capacity in a finite-blocklength setting.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to explore superactivation in the non-asymptotic regime, expanding the understanding of quantum channels' capabilities in limited uses.
AI.method: A definition for finite-blocklength superactivation is provided, alongside numerical methods for its certification.
AI.result: The study shows that using only 17 joint channel uses can facilitate qubit transmission with enhanced fidelity compared to utilizing either channel individually, indicating strong finite-blocklength superactivation.
AI.conclusion: This work paves the way for experimental demonstrations of superactivation in quantum channels under practical constraints.

title: X-Ray Spectral Variability of the TeV HBL Blazar PG 1553+113 with XMM-Newton
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ. 32 pages, 3 Main figures,3 Appendix figures and 5 tables
summary: We present an extensive X-ray spectral variability study of the TeV photon-emitting high-energy-peaked BL Lacertae object PG 1553+113, using the data from EPIC-PN camera of XMM-Newton, which observed the source during its operational period from Sep 2001 to Nov 2024. X-ray spectra in this energy range, $0.6-7.0$ keV, were fitted with absorbed Power-law (PL) and absorbed Log-Parabola (LP) models. We found with 99$\%$ confidence that 14 of them were fit well by LP models having parameters in the range $α\simeq2.13-2.80$, and $β\simeq0.04-0.18$, one spectrum favours a LP model with $β<0$, while simple PL models with $Γ\simeq2.53-2.69$ were sufficient to describe the X-ray spectra of the remaining 15. Two of these 30 observations showed strong signatures of an additional inverse Compton component, while one showed weaker indications. On fitting joint Optical Monitor and EPIC-PN data with LP models, we found synchrotron peaks in the energy range of $ν_s\simeq4.59-48.61$ eV. This indicates that the spectral evolution is probably caused by variations in particle acceleration or cooling conditions within the jet.

AI.tldr: The study investigates the X-ray spectral variability of PG 1553+113 using XMM-Newton data, revealing significant insight into particle acceleration and cooling in the jet.
AI.motivation: To understand the X-ray spectral variability and the underlying physical mechanisms in the TeV photon-emitting BL Lacertae object PG 1553+113.
AI.method: Analyzed X-ray spectra from the XMM-Newton EPIC-PN camera over multiple observations using absorbed Power-law and Log-Parabola models.
AI.result: 14 out of 30 spectra were best described by Log-Parabola models, with significant parameters found; two observations showed evidence of an inverse Compton component.
AI.conclusion: Spectral evolution likely results from changes in particle acceleration or cooling processes within the jet.

title: A theoretical account of tiny multi-Higgs vacuum expectation values from non-invertible symmetry
summary: We propose a novel mechanism to explain the naturally small vacuum expectation values (VEVs) of exotic multi-Higgs fields by employing non-invertible symmetries. Specifically, we introduce an $SU(2)_L$ quartet $H_4$ and a quintet $H_5$ within the framework of the minimal Fibonacci fusion rule (FFR). This non-invertible symmetry strictly forbids the generation of tree-level VEVs for these exotic fields. However, once the symmetry is broken, these VEVs are generated radiatively at the one-loop level.This mechanism is highly minimal, as it requires no additional loop-inducing particles. We demonstrate that for various benchmark energy scales, the resulting VEVs are naturally suppressed to the order of $10^{-3}-10^{-2}$ GeV, satisfying experimental constraints from the $ρ$ parameter. Finally, we illustrate the phenomenological viability of this setup by applying it to three representative neutrino mass models: the type-III seesaw, the Dirac neutrino seesaw, and the inverse seesaw mechanisms.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a mechanism using non-invertible symmetries to explain small vacuum expectation values (VEVs) in exotic multi-Higgs fields without additional particles.
AI.motivation: To understand naturally small VEVs of exotic Higgs fields in particle physics.
AI.method: Introduce an $SU(2)_L$ quartet $H_4$ and quintet $H_5$ constrained by minimal Fibonacci fusion rule (FFR) to forbidding tree-level VEVs, allowing loop-level generation post-symmetry breaking.
AI.result: VEVs generated radiatively at one-loop scale are suppressed to $10^{-3}-10^{-2}$ GeV, meeting constraints from the $ρ$ parameter.
AI.conclusion: The approach is phenomenologically viable, applicable to various neutrino mass models including type-III seesaw, Dirac seesaw, and inverse seesaw.

title: Non-Local Magic Resources for Fermionic Gaussian States
summary: Entanglement and magic are fundamental resources that capture the complexity of quantum many-body systems. Non-local magic isolates the irreducible nonstabilizerness intrinsically tied to entanglement. However, evaluating this quantity generally requires a prohibitive minimization over the full Hilbert space, making it computationally inaccessible beyond a few qubits. Here, we overcome this bottleneck by suggesting a closed-form expression for the non-local stabilizer entropies of fermionic Gaussian states over local Gaussian unitaries, which can be evaluated in polynomial time directly from the eigenvalues of the reduced Majorana covariance matrix. We apply this framework to characterize fermionic non-local magic across diverse physical regimes: we derive an exact Page-like curve for typical random states, reveal logarithmic scaling at the quantum critical point of the XY model, and establish a quasiparticle picture for magic generation during out-of-equilibrium quantum quenches. Crucially, because our result relies solely on two-point correlation functions, it provides a scalable route for the experimental estimation of fermionic non-local magic in large-scale quantum processors via fermionic shadow tomography.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a polynomial-time method to evaluate non-local magic for fermionic Gaussian states, overcoming computational challenges associated with quantum many-body systems.
AI.motivation: The complexity of quantum many-body systems requires effective measures for capturing entanglement and magic, especially given the computational inaccessibility of traditional methods.
AI.method: The authors propose a closed-form expression for non-local stabilizer entropies of fermionic Gaussian states, computable from the eigenvalues of the reduced Majorana covariance matrix.
AI.result: They derive results including a Page-like curve for random states, logarithmic scaling at a quantum critical point, and a quasiparticle model for magic generation in quantum quenches.
AI.conclusion: This approach enables experimental estimation of fermionic non-local magic in large-scale quantum processors, leveraging the simplicity of two-point correlation functions.

title: Dark photon search status in $τ-c$ energy region
comment: Contribution to The 7th International Workshop on Future Tau-Charm Facilities (FTCF2025)
summary: The dark photon plays an important role as a portal to dark matter and has been extensively studied on both experimental and theoretical frontiers. However, as no signals have been observed, the whereabouts of the dark photon remain a long-standing open question. With the proposal of a future $τ-c$ facility, this proceeding reviews and summarizes the current experimental status of the dark photon in the $τ-c$ energy region, which is expected to provide a reference for future searches. The experimental status indicates that the dark photon in the $τ-c$ energy region remains highly promising, highlighting the requirement for larger data samples or new methods to further investigate the benchmarks related to the observed cosmic dark matter.

AI.tldr: The paper reviews the experimental status of dark photons, particularly in the τ-c energy region, suggesting its potential for future dark matter detection.
AI.motivation: To address the open question of dark photon existence and its implications for dark matter research.
AI.method: Summary of current experimental findings at the τ-c facility and analysis of dark photon search strategies.
AI.result: The τ-c energy region shows promising potential for dark photon searches, albeit without confirmed signals.
AI.conclusion: Larger data samples and innovative methods are necessary for advancing investigations into the connection between dark photons and cosmic dark matter.

title: Resolving spurious topological entanglement entropy in stabilizer codes
summary: Topological entanglement entropy (TEE) is a key diagnostic of long-range entanglement in two-dimensional gapped phases of matter, but it can suffer from spurious contributions that overestimate the total quantum dimension of the underlying topological order.
